metadata.description: Personal, portable toolkit of reusable Claude systems: skills, rules, hooks, and templates shared across every project and device.

plugins.name: project-init
plugins.description: Three skills: project-init offers the Git-native work-tracker and portable second-brain knowledge vault during new-project setup; project-sync audits existing projects and safely adopts, health-checks, or migrates approved toolkit systems; machine-sync sets up a whole computer, installing the machine-wide rules, settings, and hooks that have to hold in every repository.

plugins.name: sf-architect-solutioning
plugins.description: Salesforce solution architect skill: pushes back on vague requirements, verifies platform facts against official Salesforce docs (live fetch, never memory), designs declarative-first to Well-Architected standards, and produces an approved solution plan before any build.

plugins.name: second-brain
plugins.description: Portable Git-native project knowledge for Claude, Codex, and optional Obsidian, with fixed properties, project tags, visible provenance, read-only health reports, owner-approved workflows, read-only Claude Code session search, and safe migration.

plugins.name: git-workflows
plugins.description: Three parallel-session-safe git lifecycle skills. pull-latest updates without rewriting history, reset-to-remote mirrors a remote behind explicit confirmation, and merge-and-clean-up lands an approved pull request before safely removing only its branch and worktree.

plugins.name: hooks-library
plugins.description: Hooks that make a rule land mechanically instead of restating it. style-reminder re-states the project's active output style every time the owner sends a message, so the voice instructions never go stale hours into a session. writing-guard reads the finished reply and blocks on an em dash or a section sign, so a slip is caught rather than shipped. no-ai-attribution-guard refuses any commit or pull request whose text credits an AI, on every repository on the machine.

plugins.name: grill-me
plugins.description: Relentless discovery interview skill that asks one question at a time, recommends a likely answer, and checkpoints every response to a durable brainstorm file before continuing.

plugins.name: work-tracker
plugins.description: Git-native work tracking shared by Claude and Codex, with deterministic status, handoffs, relationships, Git landing verification, generated dashboards, and optional GitHub Issues and Projects synchronization.

plugins.name: handoff
plugins.description: Ends a long session without losing what it learned. Invokes the project's remember workflow when available, waits for owner approval, then drafts a self-contained prompt for a fresh session that opens with the goal and carries anything not saved. A second agent checks the prompt against the repository before the owner sees it.

plugins.name: session-summary
plugins.description: Recaps a session as a table, one row per main request the owner made, in the owner's own words and in the order asked, each carrying an honest status: done, done unverified, partly done, blocked, waiting on you, not started, dropped, or answered. A block below the table names whatever still needs the owner.

plugins.name: explain-simply
plugins.description: Re-explains the last answer, a plan, or any file the owner names as short bullets grouped under bold headings, at a reading level anyone follows in one pass. Every number, date, file path and person's name survives, because a simple explanation that dropped the facts is not simpler, only vaguer. Reads the project's active output style first so the plain version sounds like the rest of the project, and ends with a numbered list of what the owner has to do, only when there is something to do.

plugins.name: track-tasks
plugins.description: Keeps every topic still open in the current session on Claude Code's built-in task list, including the ones easiest to lose: topics the owner parked, questions they have not answered, and work blocked behind something else. Marks an item finished only when it actually is, and says plainly when something has to move to the work tracker or a handoff prompt to survive the session ending. Ships with the track-open-topics rule, which is what makes a session keep the list without being asked.
